code_quality.description: Backup file committed to version control. Contains broken/incomplete Go code (unclosed braces, duplicate UpdateFailureHistory call) and will confuse reviewers about the canonical implementation. `.bak` files are development artifacts that must never be checked in.

Partial-recovery path detects a stale non-compiling test file (alreadyWritten=true, compilesSuccessfully=false) but takes no action: it does not delete the broken file from disk and does not remove its entry from the in-memory manifest before falling through to the retry loop. The spec explicitly requires: 'If it exists but does not compile, it is deleted and re-written.' As written, the retry loop will write a new file and append a SECOND entry for the same scenario name to the manifest (line 156-158), leaving the stale broken file on disk. On subsequent retries the same scenario accumulates duplicate manifest entries indefinitely.
code_quality.suggested_fix: After the compilesSuccessfully check fails (line 132), before falling through: (1) call os.Remove(filepath.Join(s.cfg.WorkDir, testFile)) to delete the stale file, and (2) rebuild manifest.Scenarios filtering out entries with Name == scenario.Name, then call saveManifest to persist the cleanup.

code_quality.description: The replan handler builds `var annotated []string` with an inline ~30-line loop that re-implements the same prefix checks and hint format as the exported `AnnotateWithPersistentHints` function defined in failure_history.go:72. The two implementations can drift independently. The spec says this logic should live in helper functions (implying a single authoritative implementation).
code_quality.suggested_fix: Replace the inline loop (lines 151-181) with a single call: `rs.ReplanContext = AnnotateWithPersistentHints(replanContext.Failures, rs.FailureHistory, 2)`

code_quality.description: `extractFailureKeys` (unexported) is defined but never called from production code. The replan handler at lines 133-139 re-implements the same key-extraction merge inline instead of calling this helper. The function only exists in test code paths, making it dead production code.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Delete `extractFailureKeys` and replace the inline merge in the replan handler (lines 133-139) with a call to this helper, or simply inline the call to `AnnotateWithPersistentHints` which subsumes both the extraction and the annotation.

code_quality.description: `compilesSuccessfully` (line 296) and `getCompileError` (line 309) each independently run `go test -c -o /dev/null <pkgPath>`. On every compile failure the package is compiled twice: once to detect the failure and once to collect error output. For packages with many files this doubles compilation cost per retry attempt (up to 6 compiler invocations for a scenario with 2 retries).
code_quality.suggested_fix: Merge the two functions into one that runs the command once, captures combined output, and returns both a bool and the error string. E.g. `func (s *WriteScenarioTestsStage) compile(testFilePath string) (ok bool, errors string)`.

code_quality.description: The file has a `//go:build integration` build tag, but the spec's validation command (`go test ./internal/next/specloop/ -count=1 -run TestIntegration`) does not include `-tags integration`. This silently skips all four integration tests, including coverage of pipeline stage ordering, idempotency across replan cycles, persistent failure hints, and ScenarioTestsWritten persistence. The acceptance criteria (AC #13: 'all existing pipeline tests continue to pass') is never exercised for these behaviors.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Either remove the `//go:build integration` tag so these tests run with `go test ./...`, or document the required build tag in the validation commands and CI configuration.

code_quality.description: `docs/scenario-tests.md` is resolved via `os.ReadFile("docs/scenario-tests.md")` relative to the process's current working directory, not relative to `p.cfg.WorkDir`. If `gromit-next` is invoked from any directory other than the project root (e.g., from a CI runner, a subdirectory, or a worktree path), the file silently won't be found and the LLM generates tests without the Seed/Invoke/Assert pattern guidance. The spec requires this content to be wired as system prompt guidance at adapter construction time.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Resolve the path relative to `p.cfg.WorkDir`: `patternsPath := filepath.Join(p.cfg.WorkDir, "docs/scenario-tests.md")`

code_quality.description: `TestWriteScenarioTests_CompileFailureSelfRepair` is titled to verify that self-repair succeeds after an initial compile failure. However, `WorkDir` is set to `t.TempDir()` — a directory with no `go.mod`. `go test -c` always fails in this context regardless of file content, so the stage falls through to the empty-path no-op (returnedPaths exhausted) and returns `Continue`. The test passes, but not because self-repair succeeded — it passes because the compilation check never distinguishes success from failure. The behavior under test is not actually verified.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Either use the project root as WorkDir (following the pattern of other tests in this file) and write a test file at a real compilable package path, or split the test into a unit test that mocks the compile check.

code_quality.description: The `contains(s, substr string) bool` helper reimplements `strings.Contains` with a hand-rolled loop. Using a custom implementation instead of the standard library is unnecessary and slightly misleading to readers who expect idiomatic Go.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Delete the `contains` function and replace all usages with `strings.Contains`.

code_quality.description: `os.Getenv("PWD")` with a `"."` fallback is used in three test functions (lines 193, 525, 646) to locate the project root for compilation checks. `PWD` is not guaranteed to be set in all execution environments (CI, `go test -vet`, invocations from subdirectories). The fallback `"."` resolves to the wrong directory when tests are run from a subdirectory, causing compilation checks to fail or pass for the wrong reason.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Use `filepath.Abs("..")` from the test file's known location, or call `os.Getwd()` which is always available in Go test processes.

code_quality.description: `"log"` is imported solely for one `log.Printf` warning when `docs/scenario-tests.md` is missing. All other diagnostic output in this file uses `fmt.Errorf` or is silent. Mixing `log` with `fmt` for a single optional warning is inconsistent and makes it harder to suppress or redirect output in tests.
code_quality.suggested_fix: Either use `fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "warning: ...")` for consistency with the file's style, or remove the warning entirely since the missing-file case is handled gracefully by proceeding with an empty patterns string.

spec_alignment.description: Backup file committed (or present as untracked) in version control. Contains broken/incomplete Go syntax (unclosed brace, duplicate UpdateFailureHistory call) and will confuse reviewers about the canonical implementation.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Delete the file: `rm internal/next/specloop/specloop.go.bak` and ensure it is not committed.

spec_alignment.description: Re-run recovery path detects a stale non-compiling test file but takes no action — it does not delete the file or remove it from the manifest before proceeding to the retry loop. The spec explicitly requires: 'If it exists but does not compile, it is deleted and re-written.' The code falls out of the `if alreadyWritten` block (line 128-133) without cleaning up, so the broken file persists. If the writer then returns an empty path (e.g., noop writer), the stale file remains forever. Note: the diff proposes adding stale-file cleanup with `os.Remove`, but that code is not present in the current file on disk.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: After the `compilesSuccessfully` check fails, delete the stale file and remove its entry from the manifest before proceeding to the retry loop: `os.Remove(filepath.Join(s.cfg.WorkDir, testFile))` (use WorkDir-relative resolution for relative paths).

spec_alignment.description: The replan handler inlines the persistent-failure annotation logic (~30 lines, `var annotated []string` loop) rather than calling the exported `AnnotateWithPersistentHints` function defined in failure_history.go:72. The two implementations can drift if the threshold, prefix checks, or message format changes. The spec states this logic should live in helper functions (implying a single authoritative implementation).
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Replace the inline annotation loop with a call to `AnnotateWithPersistentHints(replanContext.Failures, rs.FailureHistory, 2)` and assign the result to `rs.ReplanContext`.

spec_alignment.description: `extractFailureKeys` (unexported helper at line 218) is defined but never called in production code. The replan handler calls `ExtractTestFailureKeys` and `ExtractContractFailureKeys` directly via inline merge (lines 132-139) rather than using this helper. If the inline duplication is fixed by calling `AnnotateWithPersistentHints`, this helper becomes fully dead code.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Replace lines 132-139 with a call to `extractFailureKeys(replanContext.Failures)`, or remove the helper entirely if the inline logic is consolidated into `AnnotateWithPersistentHints`.

spec_alignment.description: `compilesSuccessfully` (line 296) and `getCompileError` (line 309) each independently run `go test -c -o /dev/null <pkgPath>`. On every compile failure the package is compiled twice: once to detect failure and once to collect error output. For packages with many files this doubles compilation cost per retry attempt.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Combine into a single method `runCompile(testFilePath string) (ok bool, output string)` that returns both the success flag and the combined output, then call it once per attempt.

spec_alignment.description: `TestIntegration_PersistentFailureHintAfterTwoCycles` asserts `rs.Status == runstore.StatusNeedsHuman` after 3 cycles are exhausted with a review stage that always returns `ReplanFrom`. When cycles are exhausted with a pending replan, the specloop sets `StatusBlocked` (confirmed by `TestSpecLoop_CycleExhaustion_SetsBlockerSummaryFromReplanContext` in specloop_test.go). `StatusNeedsHuman` is only set when a stage explicitly returns the `NeedsHuman` action. This assertion will fail at runtime.

The file has a `//go:build integration` build tag, but the spec's validation command `go test ./internal/next/specloop/ -count=1 -run TestIntegration` does not include `-tags integration`. This means the integration tests are silently skipped by both `go test ./...` (AC #13) and by the spec's own validation commands. The tests cover critical behaviors: stage ordering, idempotency across replan cycles, persistent failure hints, and ScenarioTestsWritten persistence.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Either remove the `//go:build integration` tag so the tests run by default, or update the spec's validation commands and CI configuration to include `-tags integration`.

spec_alignment.description: `TestWriteScenarioTests_CompileFailureSelfRepair` sets `WorkDir` to `t.TempDir()` — a directory without a `go.mod` file. `go test -c -o /dev/null ./evidence` always fails regardless of file content, so the test 'passes' because the retry loop exhausts `returnedPaths` and falls through to the empty-path no-op, not via genuine compilation success. The test title and comment claim to verify self-repair, but the behavior under test is never actually exercised.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Set `WorkDir` to a directory that is a valid Go module root (e.g., the actual project root via `runtime` or an environment variable), or mock the compilation check to control pass/fail outcomes independently of the filesystem.

spec_alignment.description: `docs/scenario-tests.md` is resolved via `os.ReadFile("docs/scenario-tests.md")` relative to the process CWD, not relative to `p.cfg.WorkDir`. If `gromit-next` is invoked from any directory other than the project root, the file will silently not be found and the LLM will generate tests without the Seed/Invoke/Assert pattern guidance. The spec requires this content to be wired at adapter construction time as system prompt guidance.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Use `filepath.Join(p.cfg.WorkDir, "docs/scenario-tests.md")` to resolve the path relative to the configured working directory.

spec_alignment.description: The custom `contains(s, substr string) bool` function reimplements `strings.Contains` using a hand-rolled loop. This is unnecessary and slightly misleading to readers who expect standard library usage.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Delete the `contains` helper and replace all call sites with `strings.Contains`.

spec_alignment.description: `os.Getenv("PWD")` with a `"."` fallback is used in three test functions to locate the project root for compilation checks. `PWD` is not guaranteed to be set in all execution environments (CI, `go test -vet`, invocations from subdirectories). The fallback `"."` may silently resolve to the wrong directory, causing compilation checks to fail or pass unexpectedly.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Use `filepath.Abs(".")` or derive the module root via `go env GOMOD` / `runtime/debug.ReadBuildInfo()` to obtain a reliable project root path.

spec_alignment.description: The three new fields (`ContractsWritten`, `ScenarioTestsWritten`, `FailureHistory`) drop the column-aligned formatting used by every other field in the RunState struct. Every other field uses a consistent tab-aligned style; these three use compact one-per-line declarations without alignment, making the struct harder to scan.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Align the three new fields to match the existing tab-stop formatting in the struct.

spec_alignment.description: `"log"` is imported solely for one `log.Printf` warning when `docs/scenario-tests.md` is missing. All other diagnostic output in this file uses `fmt.Errorf` or is silent. Mixing `log` with `fmt` for a single case is inconsistent and makes output harder to control in tests.
spec_alignment.suggested_fix: Replace `log.Printf("warning: ...")` with a silent no-op or surface the warning through the existing structured logging/event mechanism used elsewhere in the file.
